page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The system is provisioned with 24 dedicated virtual CPUs backed by 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is allocated at 48.0 GB, resulting in a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic suites such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier of multi-core and general compute performance. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 11562.0, a PassMark CPU score of 29354.86, and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 23298.44. For memory throughput, uncached large-block reads register at 129.31 GB/sec and writes at 63.06 GB/sec. While most inference metrics remain average, text generation throughput on small 135M language models shows upper-quartile performance at 298.93 tokens per second, aided by onboard vector instruction support.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent data to reside on external network volumes. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The balance of high dedicated CPU count against modest memory makes it resource-efficient for CPU-bound tasks where large memory footprints are not required. It is designed for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving clusters, batch processing, and CPU-based data parsing.

Operating on x86_64 architecture under KVM, it provides 48.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The processor features AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI instructions alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-core performance, recording 29354.86 in PassMark CPU and 11562.0 in Geekbench multi-core, with strong throughput on small-model text generation. The configuration is appropriate for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration, web serving, and distributed batch processing.
